name: Raw talking head
summary: One take to camera, cut tight, captions and a frame-1 header. Looks unproduced on purpose.
bestFor: A strong opinion, a myth to bust or an answer to a customer question
Days with no screen recording or B-roll
The fastest format to film: one location, one take
needs: One vertical take to camera, 20 to 90 seconds of usable speech

modes.use: The whole video. Face-aware framing keeps the eyes about 40% from the top.

overlaySlots.when: Frame 1 to about 3 s: the hook as a header, so frame 1 works as the thumbnail.
Optional, once, after the hook: who is talking and why they know.

notes: First spoken word within 0.3 s of frame 1.
Cut only flubs, retakes and dead air. Keep every finished sentence whole.
Drop a weak point rather than pad the length.
No baked-in music: the user adds a trending sound in the app.

evidence.why: Most skips happen in the first 3 seconds, and frame 1 is also the thumbnail. A visible claim gives a reason to stay.
Viewers hear pauses as dead air; tight cuts measurably keep people watching in short-form tests.

evidence.choice: Subtle punch-ins only at jump cuts
evidence.why: A 6 to 10% zoom change hides the jump without looking produced.
A trending sound added in the app reaches more people and avoids licensing problems.

evidence.choice: Fillers, restarts and stutters cut; a breath kept at full stops
evidence.why: Dead air and false starts read as hesitation; a tiny pause after a full stop keeps the delivery human instead of breathless.
